evals.name: dashboard-figures-count-up
evals.prompt: The dashboard feels dead when it loads, the four numbers just pop in. Make the figures count up and have the cards come in nicely.
evals.expected_output: On first load the four cards enter with transform and opacity only, in the same frame as the first real figures (never over the empty placeholder cards), timed from the motion tokens in src/styles/tokens.css, which are written in seconds (0.7s), so a script that reads them converts the unit. Each figure counts up once through formatStat, ending on exactly the formatted value (₹1,24,500.50, 1,284, 2.1%), while the null conversion shows n/a without animating and, when it later arrives on a refresh, never flashes NaN or n/a mid-count. The 30 second refresh does not restart the count, replay the entrance or tween the figures, since DESIGN.md says nothing moves while the figures are being read; later values are written in place. No card is visible with a blank figure, including during a stagger. The existing `transition: all 200ms` on .stat-card no longer drives the animated properties, figures use tabular numerals as docs/design/DESIGN.md requires, the aria-live region on #stats does not announce every frame and each figure's text appears once, and reduced motion (tokens at 0s, CSS and the script) shows the final state at once with no division by a zero duration. New tests pin an intermediate frame and the exact end value, make check passes, no dependency or build step is added, nothing is committed, and the final message says which browser checks were not run.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and it runs new tests of the count-up beyond the four in test/format.test.js: at least one asserts that a frame shown partway through the count is exactly equal to formatStat(stat, v) for the intermediate value v that frame represents (compared with assert.equal against formatStat's output, or against a literal that equals it; a regular-expression or shape check does not pass), and at least one asserts the last frame equals formatStat(stat, value) exactly

On first load each of the three numeric figures counts up and its final text is exactly what formatStat returns for the real value (with the fixture's SAMPLE: ₹1,24,500.50, 1,284 and 2.1%), and every value shown during the count is formatted with formatStat for the same stat (no raw floats, no lost ₹ sign or Indian grouping)
A null figure (conversion is null in SAMPLE and until mid-morning per src/api.js) shows n/a and is not animated; the count-up never shows NaN, undefined or ₹0.00 for it

When a figure that was null on an earlier load becomes a number on a later refresh (conversion arriving mid-morning), the code never interpolates from null: it shows the new value at once or counts from 0, so no frame reads NaN or n/a on the way; judged from the code path, or from a test that covers it

The 30 second refresh in src/dashboard.js (REFRESH_MS, setInterval(load, ...)) neither restarts the counts nor replays the card entrance, and, because docs/design/DESIGN.md says the figures are what people read so nothing moves while they are being read, a refresh does not count or tween a figure at all: only the first render of real figures animates, and later values are written in place (a run that animates the change from the previous value to the new one on every refresh fails this unless its final message names the DESIGN.md rule and asks the user whether to keep it)

The card entrance is tied to the first render of real figures (fetched stats or the SAMPLE fallback): the cards do not play their entrance on page open over the empty   placeholders and then have the numbers appear later; entrance and count start together when the data is rendered

Where the script reads a duration from the motion tokens, it handles the unit the fixture uses: tokens.css writes durations in seconds (--duration-deliberate: 0.7s), so the count lasts about 0.7 s, not 0.7 ms (a bare parseFloat of '0.7s' used as milliseconds fails this) and not 700 s; a run that mirrors the token in a named millisecond constant with the correct value passes. The whole count takes no longer than about 1 second

With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (which sets every duration token to 0s) the script writes each final formatted value at once without dividing by a zero duration (no NaN or Infinity progress, no frame that never finishes), and the cards appear in their final place with opacity 1; no card or figure stays hidden or at its starting value

The card entrance animates only transform and opacity (no top, margin, height, width or box-shadow in the entrance), and no `transition: all` remains on an element the run animates (the fixture's `transition: all 200ms ease` on .stat-card is replaced or narrowed so it does not also retime the entrance; listing the hover properties explicitly is fine)

Durations and easings of the new motion come from the motion tokens in src/styles/tokens.css (var(--duration-*) and var(--ease-*) in CSS; in the script, read from the custom property at runtime or a constant that names the token it mirrors; an easing function in the script commented as approximating --ease-* passes), not new unexplained time literals

The figures do not change width while counting: .stat-value (or the element holding the number) uses tabular numerals (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums or font-feature-settings 'tnum') as docs/design/DESIGN.md requires, or the run shows another way the width is fixed

Screen readers are not sent every intermediate value: the aria-live region on #stats in index.html is handled during the count (for example aria-busy while counting, or the live region off during the count, or the animated digits aria-hidden with the final value exposed), the final values remain available to assistive technology, and once the count has ended each card's figure appears exactly once in its text content (a second copy that exists only while the count runs and is removed when it ends passes; a visible aria-hidden copy plus a visually hidden copy of the same number that both stay after the count, which copy and paste picks up twice, fails this)

The cards and figures still end in their final visible state if the script's animation does not run (for example the entrance starts from a class the script adds, or the CSS end state is the default), so a failed or skipped animation never leaves a card invisible
package.json gains no dependency, no build step or bundler is added, and no animation library is loaded from a CDN

src/format.js and src/api.js keep their behaviour (formatStat returns the same strings; the four existing tests still pass unchanged), and the motion tokens in src/styles/tokens.css are not rewritten into milliseconds to suit the script
The final message does not claim the animation was seen or checked in a browser unless the transcript shows a browser run; if none ran, it says that visual and browser checks were not run
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree

No card is ever visible with an empty figure: from the moment a card's opacity rises above 0 (including cards waiting out a stagger delay) its .stat-value already holds a formatted figure, the count's starting value or n/a, never the fixture's   placeholder; judged from the code and CSS, or from a browser sample the run took
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: task-row-complete-and-expand
evals.prompt: Completing a task feels abrupt, the row just vanishes. Can you animate it, check mark and then the row goes away smoothly? Also the notes expander on each row stutters on Android, fix that while you're in there.
evals.expected_output: An Expo (React Native 0.76) app judged by reading the code, since node_modules are absent and jest-expo, tsc and the app cannot run here (pnpm-workspace.yaml makes pnpm scripts refuse to run without installed dependencies). Completing a task shows the check, holds it for at least motion.duration.fast, then the row leaves with opacity or transform on the native driver (or LayoutAnimation) while the rows below close the gap. The task is completed even if the animation is cut short, a second tap on the same row does nothing, and two rows tapped in quick succession both complete. The undo bar appears no later than the row starts to leave, Undo brings the row back fully visible, and the handler finds the completed task from the store rather than a stale render's list. The notes expander no longer animates height on the JS thread with useNativeDriver false and no longer clips notes at a hard-coded 120, so the long block B note is readable. No native package such as react-native-reanimated or moti is added, because ADR-0003 forbids native modules before 2.4 and the app ships over EAS Update. Durations and easings come from src/theme.ts, not DESIGN.md's stale 200 ms. Both the OS reduce-motion setting and the in-app Reduce animations setting remove the movement while keeping the end state, including the check mark. Completion is announced to screen readers and the checkbox reports checked while the check shows, tests are added with the final message saying they were not run, and nothing is committed.
expectations: Completing a task animates: the checkbox shows its checked state (a check mark or fill), the check is held fully visible for at least about motion.duration.fast (150 ms) before the row starts to leave, and the row then leaves with a fade, slide or scale while the rows below move up into the gap instead of jumping; judged from app/index.tsx, src/components/TaskRow.tsx and any new component

The completion and exit animations run on the native side: Animated calls on opacity or transform use useNativeDriver: true, or the removal uses LayoutAnimation (called in the same tick as the state change that removes the row); nothing in the completion path animates height, margin or padding with useNativeDriver: false
The notes expander in src/components/TaskRow.tsx no longer runs Animated.timing on height with useNativeDriver: false (the fixture's 300 ms timing at toValue 120)

Expanded notes are not clipped to a hard-coded height: the long note on task t2 (block B meter reading, several sentences) is fully readable when expanded, because the height is measured or the content is laid out at its natural size rather than capped at 120

package.json gains no package with native code (for example react-native-reanimated, moti, react-native-gesture-handler, lottie-react-native) and no existing dependency is upgraded, respecting docs/adr/0003-no-native-changes-before-2-4.md; the work uses React Native core Animated, LayoutAnimation or what is already installed

The final message or transcript shows the run noticed the ADR-0003 constraint (or the dev-client and EAS Update setup in README.md and app.json) when choosing how to animate; a run that adds a native package, or plans one without mentioning the constraint, fails this

Durations and easings in the changed code come from motion in src/theme.ts (motion.duration.* and motion.easing.*), with no new millisecond literals in the components (a LayoutAnimation built with a token duration and one of its preset curves passes, since it cannot take a bezier), and the run does not follow the stale '200 ms ease-in-out, no animation on the list' line in docs/design/DESIGN.md

The OS reduce-motion setting is honoured: the code reads AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled and follows changes (the reduceMotionChanged listener or a hook built on it), and with it on the row is removed and the notes open without movement (a cut or a plain fade), while the checkbox still shows its checked state for at least about motion.duration.fast (150 ms) before the row goes or starts to fade (removing the row instantly, or starting its fade in the same frame the check appears, fails this, since the request asked for the check mark and a check nobody can see does not answer it)
The in-app 'Reduce animations' setting from src/settings/SettingsContext.tsx (useSettings().reduceAnimations) is honoured by the same code path as the OS setting, so either one turns the movement off
With either reduce setting on, the end state is unchanged: the task is still completed and removed from the list, the undo bar still appears, and the notes still expand to their full text

The completion is committed even when its animation does not finish: completeTask is not called only inside an animation callback guarded by `finished` (an interrupted animation, a recycled or unmounted row, or leaving the screen must not lose the completion or leave the row half faded), a second tap on the same row while its animation runs does not complete it twice or restart the animation, and two different rows tapped in quick succession both end up completed

Completing a task is announced to screen readers (for example AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility, or accessibilityLiveRegion on the undo bar), since the row's disappearance alone carries that meaning

The checkbox's accessibilityState reports checked from the moment the check mark shows, not only after the row is removed from the store (the fixture derives it from task.done, which stays false until completeTask runs)

Tests are added or updated under __tests__/ or beside the component for the reduce-motion decision (OS setting and in-app setting) and for completion with the animation in place (the task ends up completed, including when the animation is cut short or undone), and the existing store tests in __tests__/tasks.test.ts are not weakened

The final message says that the tests, the type check and the app were not run (no node_modules, and pnpm-workspace.yaml makes pnpm scripts refuse to run without them), unless the transcript shows them running, and does not claim the stutter was verified fixed on a device; no dependency install was run and no node_modules or lockfile is left in the output repository

No file outside the task list, its row and undo components, the settings or theme modules, a new motion helper, tests and docs was changed (app.json, babel.config.js, pnpm-workspace.yaml and the store's completion semantics are unchanged unless the final message says why)
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree

The undo bar does not wait for the whole exit animation: it appears no later than the moment the row starts to leave, its 4 second window (UNDO_MS in app/index.tsx) counts from when it appears, and tapping Undo, whether during the exit or after it, brings the task's row back fully visible and pressable (not left at the exit animation's opacity, offset or scale, and not completable only after a remount); a run that deliberately delays the bar passes only if its final message tells the user the undo bar now appears later and by how much

The completion handler does not rely on a task list captured by an earlier render: the task the undo bar names and restores is looked up from the store at the moment of completion (for example getOpenTasks(), the task passed in by the row, or a ref kept current), so when two rows are completed in quick succession, or the list changes while an exit animation runs, the undo bar names and Undo restores the task that was actually completed last
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
